101.ItemDesExchange: Their body is gray, with a silvery gray belly and off-white fins. They are settled, non-migratory fish that enjoy resting in plant-rich and muddy waters, and feed mostly on snails. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
101.ItemDes: Its body is a soft silver-gray, with a faint moonlight-like sheen across its belly and pale fins. As it swims, tiny glimmers ripple across the surface, giving it a calm, crystal-clear beauty.

102.ItemDesExchange: This species of surfperch has stripes on its body, and migrates between the deep and shallow areas of offshore waters throughout the year. They are usually solitary and feed mostly on snails. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
102.ItemDes: Its stripes are sharply defined, as if painted on with care. It moves crisply, and each turn makes the stripes stand out brightly in the water.

103.ItemDesExchange: Found mostly in warmer currents, tidal silver stripes rise to the surface during the day and descend to the sea floor at night. They have silver scales on the surface of their vertical bodies, and hunt insects for food. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
103.ItemDes: Its long scales gleam with a clean brilliance, like a ribbon of light drifting across the sea. Each twist leaves behind an ethereal streak of silver.

104.ItemDesExchange: They are deep-sea fish with a long, fully black body, a small, smooth, scale-free head, and a forked tail fin. They live in warm seas, dislike intense light, and feed on insects. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
104.ItemDes: Long, slender, with a jet-black body and a forked tail, it looks like a perfectly honed dagger. It moves so quickly that more often than not, all that remains is a fleeting shadow.

105.ItemDesExchange: Their tail fin is shaped like a crescent due to moderate or severe atrophy. Typically found at the base of shallow waters amid corals and rocks, they appear in shoals and feed during the day, especially on algae. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
105.ItemDes: Its crescent-shaped tail is its signature. When the school moves as one, it looks like a painting of tiny moons swaying through the water.

106.ItemDesExchange: These herbivores have a heart-shaped tail fin and feed largely on algae. Their natural habitats are reefs located in clear waters. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
106.ItemDes: The edges of its tail fin trace a heart shape, delicate enough to look almost deliberate. It always moves with a quiet ease and is easy to spot from a distance.

107.ItemDesExchange: Found mostly in warmer currents, tidal silver stripes rise to the surface during the day and descend to the sea floor at night. They have silver scales on the surface of their vertical bodies, and hunt insects for food. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
107.ItemDes: With its muted color and sturdy form, it glides by like a silent brushstroke of ink. It never seems hurried, yet it boasts a commanding presence that naturally dominates the scene.

108.ItemDesExchange: They are deep-sea fish with a long, fully black body, a small, smooth, scale-free head, and a forked tail fin. They live in warm seas, dislike intense light, and feed on insects. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
108.ItemDes: Its scales shimmer a warm, reddish hue, like the morning glow sinking into the sea. The color is vivid but never harsh, making it hard to ignore whether in the water or on the plate.

109.ItemDesExchange: Their tail fin is shaped like a crescent due to moderate or severe atrophy. Typically found at the base of shallow waters amid corals and rocks, they appear in shoals and feed during the day, especially on algae. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
109.ItemDes: Its thick build gives it the look of something best left unprovoked. It may not be quick, but every sweep of its tail carries unmistakable weight.

110.ItemDesExchange: These herbivores have a heart-shaped tail fin and feed largely on algae. Their natural habitats are reefs located in clear waters. (This item will be retrieved automatically after the activity ends.)
110.ItemDes: It has cute little whiskers, with a look that's somehow both childlike and dignified. It may always seem a little slow-moving, but take note: cooking it is strictly forbidden.

201.ItemDes: Its slender, faintly translucent body is draped in tiger-like stripes of gold and silver. At a glance, it resembles a flicker of light, always hidden beneath the water.

202.ItemDes: With a head like a bird and fins that fan out like wings, it always looks one moment away from taking flight. What it's actually good at, though, isn't flying but skimming lightly across the surface of the sea on the wind.

203.ItemDes: With an astonishingly long tentacles lined with tiny barbs, compared to its small head and body, from afar it looks like a tangle of crawling purple threads that hardly anyone would approach with ease.

204.ItemDes: A prominent crescent mark stretches across its back, like moonlight branded into its shell. Armed with razor-sharp claws and brisk movements, it's hardly the sort you can safely pick up on a whim.

205.ItemDes: Its pale pink bell drifts like a breathing veil of mist. Strangest of all, it seems remarkably adept at "losing its head".

206.ItemDes: Plump and covered in spines, it looks like a drifting ball of fog. They're trickiest when they travel in schools, and a glance from a distance makes it hard to tell whether what's ahead is mist or a massive school of fish.

207.ItemDes: Easy to be mistaken for a tiny glowing orb clinging to the seagrass. At night, it gives off a faint green glow, like a lantern carrier beneath the calm surface.

301.ItemDes: Soaked in a warm glow, this spirit fish leaves behind soft, lavish ripples in its wake. Legend has it that it appears only when fortune is at its peak.

302.ItemDes: It may look like nothing but bare bones, but a powerful Graveborn force still dwells within. Because of this, it never truly dies, surfacing from the deep again and again.

303.ItemDes: A glimmer of moonlight and starlight rests within its broad fin-wings, so even in the deepest waters, it shines with a soft and icy radiance.

304.ItemDes: A ferocious shark with cleft wings. It charges through the sea and sometimes even rides fierce winds briefly into the air. If you ever see it above the horizon, steady your breath before you believe your eyes.

401.ItemDes: "Is this your golden axe... or your silver axe?" Neither! Just a rusty old axe!

402.ItemDes: You drag it out of the water thinking you've struck it rich. Then you open it... and it's full of sludge!

403.ItemDes: Who keeps tossing shoes into the sea? And why is it always just one?

404.ItemDes: You nearly throw out your back reeling it in, convinced you've caught some kind of sea monster. Turns out it's... this?

405.ItemDes: It looks like a treasure, and a dazzling one at that! Then the merchant takes one look and tells you it's just a regular stone the sea polished smooth!

406.ItemDes: Congratulations. After all that effort, you reel in a whole barrel of... seawater! What a haul!

501.ItemDes: You think you've caught a giant fish. What comes up instead is... something else. Do not feed it, talk to it, or make promises to it. Anything that happens after that is on you.

202648101.ItemDes: A soft blanket that keeps the cold away. It carries that warm, comforting scent of sun-dried fabric.

202648102.ItemDes: An expertly woven dreamcatcher that keeps bad dreams away from the little one.

202648103.ItemDes: Sweet, soothing nectar that makes even the most vulnerable creature feel safe and cared for.

202648104.ItemDes: Give it a light shake, and it lets out a bright little chime that calms the restless little one right down.

202648105.ItemDes: An ancient incense with a soothing scent that invokes tranquility.

202648106.ItemDes: A mysterious crystal that lulls young spirits into deep, peaceful sleep and helps them gather strength for what comes next.

202648107.ItemDes: A starlit lantern that guides lost little spirits forward toward a new beginning.

202648201.ItemDes: A plush toy as soft as a cloud, shaped like a chubby little lamb.

202648202.ItemDes: A wooden stick with a dangling ball on one end, irresistible to curious critters.

202648203.ItemDes: A delicate wind chime that rings out with a cheerful little tinkle when the breeze blows through.

202648204.ItemDes: A sweet-smelling branch with just the right amount of chew. Great for teething.

202648205.ItemDes: A softly glowing snowball that leaves a faint frosty trail as it rolls around.

202648206.ItemDes: A magical little music box that plays a soft lullaby when wound up.

202648207.ItemDes: A soft feather that leaves a light, ticklish feeling wherever it brushes.

202648208.ItemDes: A bouncy toy hammer that makes a silly little squeak every time it hits something.

202648301.ItemDes: An all-purpose shrimp bait ball that's cheap and reliable, a favorite among budget-minded anglers. The only one who hates it is probably the merchant selling premium bait.

202648302.ItemDes: The use of snail bait is controversial in the fishing community. Some people think they will damage the fishing environment; but their rich taste can attract numerous types of fish. So they are the top choice for live bait. (suitable for catching: surfperch)

202648303.ItemDes: Red worms have the most pungent fishy smell. They are suited for various fishing methods and can attract more carnivorous fish. This type of bait does not stay fresh for long, so make sure to use it as soon as you have it. (suitable for catching: striped fish)

202648304.ItemDes: As a plant-based bait, sea lettuce can be used for catching omnivorous and herbivorous sea fish. Looks like there are plenty of plant-eating fish in the sea. That's great news for the environment. (suitable for catching: surgeonfish)
